title: 41.4% of Mexican Households Supplement Income with Government Programs
author: Redacción/SinEmbargo
content:
_This article by the SinEmbargo newsroom originally appeared in the[September
22, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4874596/inegi-41-4-de-los-hogares-
mexicanos-complementa-ingresos-con-programas-de-gobierno/)._

**Mexico City, September 22 (SinEmbargo).—** The percentage of **Mexican
households** that received income from [**government
programs**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4872691/cuida-a-quien-cuida-en-cdmx-
como-funciona-el-apoyo-de-2-mil-pesos-bimestrales/) rose from 25 percent in
2020 to **41.4 percent** in 2025, according to the results of the **2025
Intercensal Survey** by the [**National Institute of Statistics and Geography
(Inegi)**](https://www.inegi.org.mx/).

This figure means that **four out of every 10 homes** reported receiving
resources from these **social programs** during the past year, in a period in
which the proportion of dwellings that obtained **income** from sources other
than work also increased.

In total, 50.1 percent of Mexican households received some extra income in
addition to labor income, compared with 38.5 percent recorded five years
earlier; among them, households with members who receive retirement benefits
or pensions also grew, rising from 13 to 16.6 percent.

Mauricio Rodríguez Abreu, Inegi’s director general of Sociodemographic
Statistics, presented these figures as part of the survey results, which make
it possible to compare changes in Mexican households between 2020 and 2025.

![A government worker in a Secretariat of Well-Being vest hands out forms to a
crowd](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/02-government-
programs.jpg)The number of households that received resources from government
programs increased 16.4 percent in five years. Photo: Daniel Augusto,
Cuartoscuro

## Social Support Reaches 41.4% of Mexican Households

Over that five-year span, the proportion of households benefiting from
government programs increased 16.4 percentage points, according to the
Intercensal Survey data.

> “Between 2020 and 2025, the proportion of households in which at least one
> member received monetary income from sources other than work increased from
> 38.5 to 50.1 percent. Specifically, households benefiting from government
> programs went from 25.0 to 41.4 percent,” Inegi detailed in its
> [communiqué](https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2026/ei/EIC2025-def_CP.pdf).

The survey also showed a decrease in other sources of income: households that
received support from people living in another dwelling within the country
went from 6.1 to 5.2 percent, while those that received money from people
living in another country fell from 5.1 to 4.7 percent.

The information comes from a sample applied from October 6 to November 14,
2025, in 7.3 million dwellings, about one in every five in the country, with
the aim of updating the national picture on population, households, migration,
education, employment, health and housing.

> [Post by @INEGI_INFORMA on
> X](https://twitter.com/INEGI_INFORMA/status/2102441423983300711)

The country closed 2025 with 130.9 million inhabitants and a median age of 32,
three years more than in 2020, of whom 130.4 million live in private
dwellings.

Although the population continued to rise, the pace of growth slowed: the
average annual rate fell to 0.7 percent between 2020 and 2025, far from the
one percent reported five years earlier. By contrast, the number of households
went from 35.2 to 39.7 million, but the average number of occupants fell from
3.6 to 3.3.

The survey also showed changes in household composition: single people
increased from 33.7 to 36.2 percent, while one-person households went from
12.4 to 15 percent.

## Women Increase Their Economic Participation

In the labor sector, 55.1 percent of the population aged 12 and older
participated in economic activity in 2025, a small gain compared with 54
percent in 2020, which was mainly due to the greater integration of women,
whose participation grew from 38.8 to 41 percent over that period.

![Women riding a Mexico City Metro car](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/03-women-metro.jpg)Women’s economic participation
increased from 38.8 to 41 percent between 2020 and 2025. Photo: Camila Ayala,
Cuartoscuro

Among the male population, by contrast, the variation was minimal, so women
came to represent almost four out of every 10 employed people nationwide.

The education sector also registered progress: school attendance grew in all
age groups, while the illiteracy rate among people aged 15 and older fell from
4.8 to 3.7 percent.

Likewise, average schooling rose to 10.3 years, which is equivalent to having
completed secondary school and the first year of upper secondary education.

## More Internet and Basic Services in Homes

The survey also recorded improvements in the coverage of basic services and in
the country’s homes: Internet access jumped, going from 53.9 to 75.7 percent
between 2020 and 2025, while the presence of cell phones increased from 88.1
to 94.5 percent.

[Inegi communiqué: 2025 Intercensal Survey results (PDF, in
Spanish)](https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2026/ei/EIC2025-def_CP.pdf)

As for essential services, the proportion of homes with piped water inside
rose from 77 to 82.4 percent. By contrast, homes with no access to this
resource at all fell from 3.7 to 2.4 percent.

Regarding drainage, 79.6 percent of homes were connected to the public
network; however, 16.8 percent had a septic pit, biodigester or septic tank.

In addition, the survey measured for the first time the impact of internal
forced displacement: in **509,900 households** at least one member had to
change residence due to violence or insecurity in their locality, which
affected 1.6 million people. Another 151,900 households registered forced
displacements because of natural or human-caused disasters.
